### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/identity.json`, `packages/spec/src/identity/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e797a89764e396f75485f3b7b43d0f135aec52b`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/identity.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/identity.json`, `packages/spec/src/identity/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 41 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e797a89764e396f75485f3b7b43d0f135aec52b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6d0e1f0c0458d268fe179eaa0423b680c9ca0a1e` — the merge of head `4ce40d551df9dc9f296a2f976e9a4b7e673b3fef` into base `9e797a89764e396f75485f3b7b43d0f135aec52b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6d0e1f0c0458d268fe179eaa0423b680c9ca0a1e && git checkout 6d0e1f0c0458d268fe179eaa0423b680c9ca0a1e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9e797a89764e396f75485f3b7b43d0f135aec52b 4ce40d551df9dc9f296a2f976e9a4b7e673b3fef && git checkout -B drift-repro 9e797a89764e396f75485f3b7b43d0f135aec52b && git merge --no-ff 4ce40d551df9dc9f296a2f976e9a4b7e673b3fef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e797a89764e396f75485f3b7b43d0f135aec52b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9e797a89764e396f75485f3b7b43d0f135aec52b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4ce40d551df9dc9f296a2f976e9a4b7e673b3fef`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/identity/index.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/invitation-role-grant.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-cap.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-role-grant-offer.test.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/invitation-role-grant.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-invitation.object.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/membership-reach.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/membership-role.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/identity.json, packages/spec/export-origins/identity.json, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/es-ES.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/ja-JP.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/zh-CN.objects.generated.ts, .changeset/23957-invite-role-options-per-caller.md, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (cap call site, unchanged), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (positions projection, unchanged), packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts (unchanged), and objectui at the `.objectui-sha` pin `f8267df93a`: packages/fields/src/resolveActionParams.ts, packages/core/src/evaluator/optionRules.ts, packages/fields/src/widgets/useCascadingOptions.ts, packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.tsx, packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx, packages/app-shell/src/providers/expressionUser.ts, packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts. The scope covers all 15 changed files; no remainder is left to the lane seat's TIER_DEFAULT accept.

Inputs: card #23957 (body; triage `6219499129`, claim `6221327426`, dev report `6223402583`), PR #24033 (body, file list, net diff against merge-base `fd0e72abc2` of the head with `origin/main`), and the 41 check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-16T20:19Z: 35 success, 6 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood shards and CLI, the opt-in packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance: path-filtered or opt-in), 0 failed, 0 in progress. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, every Lint and Type Check job, and Test Core 1 to 6 plus the aggregate are among the green ones. Record written 2026-10-16T20:31Z.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The new `@objectstack/spec/identity` exports are constants and pure helpers only: right.** `invitation-role-grant.ts` exports five runtime symbols (`INVITATION_ROLE_ANY_ISSUER`, `INVITATION_ROLE_GRANTORS`, `INVITATION_ROLE_OPTIONS`, `invitationRoleGrantors`, `invitationRoleGrantPredicate`) and two types (`InvitationRoleGrantors`, `InvitationRoleOption`). It imports only its two sibling identity modules (`./membership-role`, `./eval-user.zod`), exactly as `membership-reach.ts` does, and performs no I/O and declares no schema. `api-surface/identity.json` and `export-origins/identity.json` move by exactly those seven symbols, and they are the only baselines in the repo that list identity exports (`membershipReachPredicate` appears in no other baseline).

2. **The server cap refuses exactly what it refused before, same cases, same outcomes, same text: right.** Read side by side at the merge-base and the head: `parseOrgRoles`, `orgRoleGrade`, `isOrgAdminGrade`, the empty-request return and the unresolved-issuer refusal are untouched. `isPlainMemberInvitation` is equivalent, because `member` is the only row equal to `INVITATION_ROLE_ANY_ISSUER` and an unlisted role takes the administrative row. Admission is identical by derivation: before, admitted iff issuer grade at least admin and requested grade not above it; after, `grantTableAdmits` requires issuer grade at least admin and, for each requested role, an issuer role in that row, which is `owner` only for the `owner` row and `owner` or `admin` otherwise, so an `owner` request still needs an owner issuer and every other request needs admin grade. The refused branches keep their order and their three strings byte for byte. The call site (`auth-manager.ts` `beforeCreateInvitation`, line 3415) is unchanged by the diff. The parity pin's oracle is a line-for-line freeze of the merge-base cap over a 41 by 37 grid that includes comma pairs, arrays, case and space variants and non-string values, and asserts the grid holds both refusals and admissions; Test Core is green on the head.

3. **Each option's `visibleWhen` admits exactly the issuers the cap admits for that role, on the `current_user.positions` projection the cap's grades map to: right.** The `owner` option is gated on `org_owner`, which is grade 3 in the cap; `admin` and `delegated_admin` on `org_owner` or `org_admin`, which is grade at least 2; `member` is ungated, matching the plain-member exemption. The projection is the cap's: `resolve-authz-context.ts` line 1376 splits a comma-joined `sys_member.role`, maps each name through `mapMembershipRole` (which lower-cases the three graded names, as `parseOrgRoles` does), so a multi-role issuer's positions hold every grade the cap would grade on. The offer pin does not hand-list the expected sets: for each of the three mirrors and each of the four grades it derives the admitted set from `invitationRoleCapFailure` itself and evaluates the declared `visibleWhen` with `celEngine` against `[mapMembershipRole(grade)]`. One asymmetry is inherent to the projection and is the same one the `membership-reach.ts` precedent carries: the console's positions are resolved for the active organization (or the union of memberships with none active) and may also hold a `sys_user_position` row, while the cap grades the issuer's `sys_member.role` in the target organization. The option gate is UI courtesy and the schema docblock on `visibleWhen` says so; the cap stays the authority. Not a defect of this PR.

4. **Nothing restates the rule by hand outside the table: right, with one declared exception that is not a restatement.** The three `invite_user` mirrors declare `options: [...INVITATION_ROLE_OPTIONS]` and no hand-written predicate; a grep of `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/` finds no role gate over `current_user.positions`. The cap keeps its grade ladder to grade the issuer and to choose which refusal text names the reason, and `grantTableAdmits` keeps the below-admin guard, which the table's any-issuer row cannot express. That guard changes the answer only for a duplicate-member multi-role value such as `member,member` from a delegated issuer, which the picker cannot produce; it is documented in both the table's and the cap's docblocks, and the parity pin holds it. The ladder's grade-above-issuer branch now only selects a refusal text and no longer decides admission.

5. **The dialog's labels still translate: right.** At the objectui pin, `useObjectLabel.ts` line 717 resolves `_actions.{action}.params.{param}.options.{value}` with the authored label as fallback; the CLI extractor (`i18n-extract.ts`) emits exactly that path for an action param's options; the four bundles carry it under all three mirrors; the three non-English locales reuse the field's existing strings verbatim (`受托管理员`, `委任管理者`, `Administrador delegado`, and so on); the English labels and the option order are unchanged from `BUILTIN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_OPTIONS`, which the spec pin asserts. `check:i18n` runs in `lint.yml` and the Lint check-runs are green.

6. **No objectui half is needed (the PR's Hypothesis 1): right at `f8267df93a`, which the PR does not move.** `resolveActionParams.ts` line 650 takes authored options over inherited ones; `resolveOptionLabels` returns the list verbatim or rebuilds by spread; `normaliseOptions` (line 515) spreads too. `ActionParamDialog` renders a select param through `SelectField`, the one caller of `useCascadingOptions`, which resolves through `resolveCascadingOptions` and `resolveVisibleOptions` with the predicate scope from `ExpressionProvider`, whose `current_user` subject carries `positions: user.positions ?? []` (`expressionUser.ts` line 182). The localisation relabel (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` line 285, and `RecordDetailView.tsx` line 957) spreads each option, so `visibleWhen` survives. A faulting predicate fails open in `resolveVisibleOptions`, but a signed-out or position-less user holds `[]`, on which the gate evaluates false rather than faulting.

7. **The field-level pickers and `resend_invitation` are untouched: right.** `sys_invitation.role` keeps `[...BUILTIN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLE_OPTIONS]` with `defaultValue: member`; `sys_member.role` is unchanged; `resend_invitation` keeps its field-backed `role` with `defaultFromRow` and no options. ADR-0108 D1's closed vocabulary is not widened: the option list is the vocabulary, narrowed per caller.

### ② Semver level

The changeset declares `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, and this matches what the diff publishes: a pure widening of `@objectstack/spec/identity` by seven exports (no removal, no rename, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 marker is owed); platform metadata that moved (the three `invite_user` role params now declare gated options; the bundles carry the new keys) with values, labels and order unchanged; and a plugin-auth implementation that moved onto the table with behaviour unchanged. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is in the changeset body and `Clause-②: yes` in the PR body, consistent with AGENTS.md section 3 (`yes` takes at least `minor`). Check Changeset is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1, the admin's offer excludes Owner, against the card's done-when text.** Judged: the shipped offer is right. The cap has refused an `owner` invitation from an admin since it landed (#3722, the grade ceiling: an invitation never confers a grade above the issuer's own), the claim fixed `no change to who the server lets invite whom`, and offering Owner to an admin would reproduce for one role exactly the offer-then-refuse defect this card closes. The done-when's `an owner or admin still sees all of them` is the filer's reading of the static list, not a ruling; its second bullet, a pin asserting the offered set per caller that fails against the static list, is met for all four grades. Not escalated. For the seat: amend the card's done-when wording when closing it, so the record does not read as a deviation.
- **Open question 2, the below-admin single-member rule stays in the cap rather than the table.** Judged: acceptable as shipped. The rule is the exact-parity guard for a duplicate-member multi-role value, it is documented in both docblocks, pinned by the parity grid, and does not touch the offer. A per-row table flag would add a field with one reader. Not escalated.
- **Dev deviation, the admin offer** is open question 1 above.
- **Dev deviation, `test:repo` not run locally**: covered by Test Core 1 to 6 and the aggregate, green on the head. **`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exit 3 locally** (shallow clone): covered by the green Lint check-runs.
- **Dev deviations on process** (detaching the shared primary checkout to hold the branch in a worktree; model-free commit trailers per AGENTS.md): no content effect; nothing for this record.
- **Out-of-scope finding, carrier none**: the `ActionParam` options docblock and its `guidance` comment in `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` say objectui's `normaliseOptions` rebuilds inherited entries as `{ label, value }`; at the pin it spreads them (line 515, since `fbc23e094`). Confirmed stale; documentation drift with no runtime effect. For the seat: a docs-only card under `domain:spec` is the right carrier.
- Nothing in the diff touches who the server lets invite whom, and #23945 (the refusal's missing `code`) is untouched, as the claim required.

Reviewed-by: `session_01HjR8RUwTPQ3TgbfKihmxp9`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Reviewer of record. Every item below was checked against GitHub and the code, not against the report (`6223402583` on #23957).

- **Shape:** Draft, base `main`. The first line is `Fixes #23957`, the body's only closing keyword, then `Clause-②: yes`, matching claim `6221327426`. 15 files, +574/−29. Not governed. Assignee `os-elon-musk`.
- **What it lands:**
  - **One table, two readers.** A new `@objectstack/spec/identity` module, `invitation-role-grant.ts`, holds `INVITATION_ROLE_GRANTORS` (owner ← owner; admin and delegated_admin ← owner or admin; member ← any issuer) and pure helpers that build each option's CEL gate from it, in the shape of `membership-reach.ts`. It contains only constants and pure helpers.
  - **The cap.** `plugin-auth`'s invitation role cap decides admission from that table, with the same outcomes and the same refusal text.
  - **The mirrors.** The three `invite_user` mirrors declare `INVITATION_ROLE_OPTIONS`, each option gated by its per-option `visibleWhen`. A `delegated_admin` is offered Member only, an admin Admin / Delegated Admin / Member, an owner all four. The labels moved to `_actions.invite_user.params.role.options.*` and translate in all four locales.
- **Contract review:** PASS `6224153326` on this head (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`).
  - The cap's admission is identical by derivation, pinned against a frozen copy of the pre-table cap over a 41×37 grid.
  - Each option's gate matches the cap's grades on the real `current_user.positions` projection.
  - The baselines move by exactly the seven new symbols.
  - objectui at the pin honours an authored option's `visibleWhen` on an action param, so no objectui half is owed.
- **The report's open questions, the seat's calls:**
  - (1) An admin's picker excludes Owner: A. The cap has always refused Owner from an admin, and the claim fixed "no change to who the server lets invite whom". Showing Owner would reopen the offer-then-refuse defect for one role. The card's done-when line "an owner or admin still sees all of them" was wrong on that point; the landing record says so.
  - (2) The below-admin guard stays in the cap: A. It is pinned and documented, and it has no effect on the offer.
- **Semver:** `minor` (widening) on `@objectstack/spec`, `patch` on `platform-objects` and `plugin-auth`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.
- **CI on this head:** 41 check-runs, 35 success, 6 skipped by their filters, 0 failed. `mergeable: clean`.

At the pin it spreads them (the review and the report both measured it).
